mainTopic: Penalties in slave sales, a slave who flees into ארץ ישראל, and the limits on ransoming captives and helping them escape
overview: The amud opens by explaining why רב ענן was unsure whether money comes back in a slave sale that does not take effect. He had not heard the ברייתא that settles it, and שמואל's ruling might mean the money is a gift, as in the case of a man who betroths his sister. Next, אביי asks רב יוסף why the buyer, and not the seller, is penalized when a slave is sold outside ארץ ישראל. After the mouse-and-hole parable is challenged, the answer is that we penalize whoever holds the forbidden thing. Then רבי אמי rules that a slave who fled into ארץ ישראל must be freed, based on רבי אחי ברבי יאשיה. The גמרא lays out several readings of "לא תסגיר עבד אל אדוניו" and shows רב חסדא using one of them with the כותים. After a short story about אביי's lost donkey, a new משנה limits ransom for captives and forbids helping them escape. The גמרא asks for the reasons behind both rules and tells the story of רב עילישׁ and רב נחמן's daughters in captivity. The amud ends as a new משנה begins about buying holy objects from non-Jews, and that sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב ענן did not know the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why רב ענן had a doubt even though a ברייתא answers it: he had never heard that ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב ענן? He had not heard the ברייתא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks itself why רב ענן was unsure, since a ברייתא already answers his question. The answer is that he simply did not know that ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, a ברייתא was brought that settles whether the money is returned. That raises a problem: how could רב ענן not know the answer? The גמרא says the source never reached him, so his doubt was honest.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching of the תנאים that was not included in the משנה
He had not heard it; the source never reached him

phrases.english: And Rav Anan (why was he unsure?) –
he had not heard the baraita;

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב עָנָן בָּרַיְיתָא לָא שְׁמִיעַ לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers an unstated question carried over from the earlier discussion: why was רב ענן unsure if a ברייתא answers it?
steps.terutzResolutionType: The אמורא did not know the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since a ברייתא answers the question, רב ענן should not have had a doubt.
steps.terutzMaskana: He never heard the ברייתא, so his doubt makes sense.

steps.title: שמואל's ruling does not prove the money is returned
steps.stepSummary: Someone might think רב ענן could have answered his question from שמואל, who said the sale does not take effect. The גמרא pushes this off: perhaps שמואל holds the sale fails but the money counts as a gift.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want to settle it from שמואל: how do you know he means the sale fails and the money comes back? Maybe the sale fails and the money is a gift, just like the case of a man who tries to marry his sister.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא considers whether רב ענן could have used שמואל's ruling to answer his question. It rejects this, because שמואל's words could also mean that the money stays with the seller as a gift.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל said 'it is not sold.' That does not tell us what happens to the money. One reading is that the money goes back to the buyer. Another is that the buyer knowingly gave money for something that cannot work, so it counts as a gift. Since both readings are possible, שמואל's words leave the doubt in place.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do you know? It points out that a proof is not certain
Perhaps; it offers another possible reading
The money is treated as a gift
Just like; it compares this to another case

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree that the sale itself does not take effect. The only question is what happens to the money that was paid.

phrases.english: And if (he would settle it) from Shmuel's statement –
phrases.notes: שמואל said earlier that such a sale does not take effect.

phrases.english: from where do we know that it is not sold and the money is returned?
Perhaps it is not sold
and the money is a gift –
just as it is in the case of one who betroths his sister,
phrases.notes: קידושין to one's own sister can never take effect, so the money he gave is all that is left to discuss.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי מִדִּשְׁמוּאֵל מִמַּאי דְּאֵינָהּ מְכוּרָה וּמָעוֹת חוֹזְרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues explaining רב ענן's doubt: besides not knowing the ברייתא, he also could not settle it from שמואל.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using שמואל's ruling to settle the question about the money.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: 'It is not sold' could also mean the money stays with the seller as a gift, so it proves nothing about returning the money.

steps.title: The case of betrothing one's sister
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא cites the מחלוקת between רב and שמואל about a man who betroths his sister. רב says the money is returned; שמואל says it is a gift.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was stated: one who betroths his sister. רב says the money is returned, and שמואל says the money is a gift.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the source for the comparison it just made. It shows that שמואל really does treat money given in a deal that cannot work as a gift.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows that the 'gift' idea from the last step is not just a guess about שמואל. In the sister case he openly says the money is a gift. So when שמואל says a slave sale 'is not sold,' he might hold the same thing there, and רב ענן could not rely on him.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was stated; it introduces a recorded מחלוקת of אמוראים
One who betroths his sister, a קידושין that can never take effect

steps.whyThisMatters: This מחלוקת between רב and שמואל gives a general approach to money paid in a deal that cannot take effect. שמואל holds that the payer knew it would fail, so he meant it as a gift.

phrases.english: as it was stated: one who betroths his sister –
Rav said: the money is returned;
and Shmuel said: the money is a gift.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִיתְּמַר הַמְקַדֵּשׁ אֶת אֲחוֹתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the comparison used in step 2.
steps.raayaObject: That שמואל can hold the money is a gift even when the deal fails.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The מחלוקת of רב and שמואל about one who betroths his sister.
steps.whatToRemember: רב ענן stayed unsure for two reasons. He did not know the ברייתא, and שמואל's ruling could mean the money is a gift, as in the sister case.

steps.title: אביי asks why the buyer is penalized
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רב יוסף: why does the penalty for a slave sold outside ארץ ישראל fall on the buyer? Why not penalize the seller?
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רב יוסף: Why do we penalize the buyer? Let us penalize the seller!
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. אביי questions the rule that the buyer loses out, since the seller also took part in the forbidden sale.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the rule, the buyer must free the slave and loses his money. אביי argues that the seller started the forbidden sale, so it would make sense to fine him instead, for example by making him return the money.

keyTerms.meaning: What did you see? It asks why one side was chosen over the other

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rav Yosef:
What did you see that we penalize the buyer?
phrases.notes: This is about the rule that when a slave is sold outside ארץ ישראל, the buyer must free him and loses his money.

phrases.english: Let us penalize the seller!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי לְרַב יוֹסֵף מַאי חָזֵית דְּקָנְסִינַן לְלוֹקֵחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new discussion about who carries the penalty.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that the buyer is penalized.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The seller is also guilty, so there is no clear reason to penalize the buyer rather than the seller.

steps.title: Not the mouse steals but the hole
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers with a parable: the hole, not the mouse, is the real thief. Without the buyer, the forbidden sale could not happen.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is not the mouse that steals, but the hole that steals.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף defends penalizing the buyer with a parable. A mouse only steals because it has a hole to hide things in, and the buyer is like that hole.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The seller is the mouse and the buyer is the hole. If no one were willing to buy, the seller could never sell the slave away. So the buyer is the one who makes the forbidden act possible, and he deserves the penalty.

phrases.english: He said to him:
It is not the mouse that steals,
but the hole that steals.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָאו עַכְבְּרָא גַּנָּב אֶלָּא חוֹרָא גַּנָּב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Parable showing who truly makes the wrong possible
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The seller started the sale, so he should be penalized.
steps.terutzMaskana: The buyer makes the sale possible, like a hole that lets the mouse steal, so he is penalized.

steps.title: Without the mouse, how would the hole get anything
steps.stepSummary: אביי turns the parable around: without the mouse, the hole would have nothing. The seller is just as necessary as the buyer.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If not for the mouse, where would the hole get anything from?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי rejects the parable. Both the mouse and the hole are needed, so it still does not explain why only the buyer is penalized.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The parable only shows that the buyer is needed. It does not show that he is more guilty, since the seller is needed just as much. So the question of why the buyer, and not the seller, comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: From where would it have it?

phrases.english: He said to him:
If not for the mouse,
from where would the hole have it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי לָאו עַכְבְּרָא חוֹרָא מְנָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יוסף's parable from step 5.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both the mouse and the hole are needed for the theft, so the parable does not make the buyer more guilty than the seller.

steps.title: Penalize where the forbidden thing is
steps.stepSummary: The final answer: it makes sense to penalize the one who holds the forbidden thing, and the slave is with the buyer.
steps.simpleTranslation: It stands to reason: wherever the forbidden thing is, there we penalize.
steps.whatsHappening: The discussion ends with a new reason that does not depend on who is more guilty. We penalize whoever has the forbidden item in his hands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if buyer and seller share the blame equally, the slave is now with the buyer. The way to fix the problem is to free the slave, and that can only be done by the one who has him. So the penalty falls on the buyer.

keyTerms.meaning: It stands to reason; it makes sense
The forbidden thing; here, the slave who was sold against the rule

steps.whatToRemember: The buyer is penalized not because he is more guilty, but because the forbidden thing, the slave, is in his hands.
steps.whyThisMatters: It gives a general guide for penalties: when more than one person shares the wrong, the קנס goes to the one holding the forbidden item.

phrases.english: It stands to reason:
phrases.notes: This is רב יוסף's final answer to אביי.

phrases.english: wherever the forbidden item is,
there we penalize.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִסְתַּבְּרָא הֵיכָא דְּאִיכָּא אִיסּוּרָא הָתָם קָנְסִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge from step 6 with a new reason.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The penalty falls on the buyer because the forbidden item, the slave, is with him.

steps.title: A runaway slave comes before רבי אמי
steps.stepSummary: A slave ran from חוץ לארץ to ארץ ישראל. רבי אמי told the master to free him and take a note for his value. Otherwise רבי אמי would take the slave away from him completely, based on רבי אחי ברבי יאשיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A slave ran away from outside the Land to the Land. His master followed him and came before רבי אמי. רבי אמי said: We will write you a note for the slave's value, and you write him a document of freedom. If not, I will take him away from you anyway, based on רבי אחי ברבי יאשיה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real case where a slave ran into ארץ ישראל and his master came after him. רבי אמי rules that the master must free him, and the master gets paid through a note.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אמי offers the master a fair deal: free the slave and get a note for his full value. If the master refuses, he loses the slave with no payment, because by רבי אחי ברבי יאשיה such a slave is not sent back. This sets up the next step, where the גמרא shows the source for רבי אחי's view.

keyTerms.meaning: a written note for his value (money owed)
a document that frees a slave
I will take away / cancel your ownership

phrases.english: There was a certain slave who fled
from outside the Land to the Land.
His master went after him,
and came before Rabbi Ami.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: נִכְתּוֹב לָךְ שְׁטָרָא אַדְּמֵיהּ,
phrases.english: He said to him: We will write you a note for his value,
phrases.notes: רבי אמי is speaking to the master here. The master gets a note saying the slave owes him his worth.

phrases.english: and you write him a document of freedom.
And if not, I will take him away from you
based on Rabbi Achai son of Rabbi Yoshiya.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא עַבְדָּא דַּעֲרַק מֵחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ לָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the discussion of penalizing the buyer of a slave sold to חוץ לארץ. It shifts to a slave running in the other direction.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A slave who runs from חוץ לארץ to ארץ ישראל is not returned. The master must free him and may take a note for his value.

steps.title: The ברייתא reads the פסוק as being about a גוי who leaves idol worship
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא first quotes "לא ישבו בארצך". It says one might think this includes even a גוי who gave up עבודה זרה. So it brings "לא תסגיר עבד אל אדוניו" and "עמך ישב בקרבך" to show that such a person may live in the Land.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: "They shall not dwell in your land lest they make you sin against Me." You might think this also covers a גוי who accepted not to worship idols. So the פסוק says: "Do not hand over a slave to his master who escapes to you from his master." What is his fix? "He shall dwell with you, in your midst."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the ברייתא that is the source for the opinion רבי אמי relied on. Its first reading treats the runaway 'slave' as a picture of a גוי escaping from idol worship.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "לא ישבו בארצך" bans idol worshippers from living in the Land. The ברייתא uses "לא תסגיר עבד" to show the ban does not apply to a גוי who left idolatry. In this reading he is the 'slave' running from his 'master' (his old idol worship), and he may live among us. This is the first of three readings of the same פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: as it is taught in a ברייתא
therefore the פסוק says (to teach otherwise)

steps.confusionAlert: In this first reading, the 'slave' is not a real slave at all. It is a picture of a גוי leaving his idol worship. The next steps switch to reading it as a real slave.

phrases.english: As it is taught:
"They shall not dwell in your land
lest they make you sin against Me" –
phrases.notes: שמות 23:33

phrases.english: One might think that about a gentile who accepted upon himself

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא לַעֲבוֹד עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה הַכָּתוּב מְדַבֵּר,
phrases.english: not to worship idols, the verse is speaking too,
therefore the verse says:
"You shall not hand over a slave to his master
who escapes to you from his master",
phrases.notes: דברים 23:16. Here the 'master' stands for the idol worship he ran away from.

phrases.english: What is his fix?
"He shall dwell with you, in your midst, etc."
phrases.notes: דברים 23:17

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source behind רבי אמי's reliance on רבי אחי ברבי יאשיה.
steps.raayaObject: The opinion of רבי אחי ברבי יאשיה that רבי אמי relied on
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading דברים 23:16-17 (לא תסגיר עבד אל אדוניו)

steps.title: רבי יאשיה: the word "his master" does not fit
steps.stepSummary: רבי יאשיה objects to the first reading. If the פסוק meant a גוי leaving idol worship, it should have said "from his father", not "from his master".
steps.simpleTranslation: This was difficult for רבי יאשיה: "From his master"?! It should have said "from his father"!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יאשיה challenges the first reading of the פסוק. He points to one word that does not fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person's religion is something he grew up with from his family. So a picture of leaving it should speak of a 'father', not a 'master'. Because the פסוק says 'master', רבי יאשיה thinks it must mean a real slave and a real master.

keyTerms.meaning: and it was difficult for him

phrases.english: And it was difficult for Rabbi Yoshiya:
This "from his master"?!
It should have said "from his father"!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְקַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יֹאשִׁיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ברייתא's reading of the פסוק as being about a גוי.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of "עבד ... מעם אדוניו" as a גוי leaving עבודה זרה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'master' does not fit a picture of leaving one's religion. 'Father' would have fit better.

steps.title: רבי יאשיה: the פסוק is about selling a slave to חוץ לארץ
steps.stepSummary: רבי יאשיה gives a new reading. The פסוק is about a master who sells his slave to someone in חוץ לארץ. Such a slave is not handed over and stays in the Land.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי יאשיה said: The פסוק is speaking about someone who sells his slave to outside the Land.
steps.whatsHappening: Having rejected the first reading, רבי יאשיה offers his own. The פסוק is about a real slave who was sold to a master in חוץ לארץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now 'master' means an actual master, which solves רבי יאשיה's problem. In this reading, "do not hand him over" means we do not send him to the new owner abroad. He stays in ארץ ישראל. This ties back to the earlier steps about a slave sold to חוץ לארץ.

keyTerms.meaning: one who sells his slave to outside the Land

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Yoshiya said:
About one who sells his slave to outside the Land
the verse is speaking.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יֹאשִׁיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the reading that was just challenged with a new one.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק is a picture of a גוי leaving idol worship.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק is about a real slave sold to a master in חוץ לארץ.

steps.title: רבי אחי: the words "escapes to you" do not fit
steps.stepSummary: רבי אחי ברבי יאשיה objects to his father's reading. A slave sold to חוץ לארץ is leaving the Land, so the פסוק should have said "escapes from you", not "escapes to you".
steps.simpleTranslation: This was difficult for רבי אחי ברבי יאשיה: "Who escapes to you"?! It should have said "who escapes from you"!
steps.whatsHappening: Now רבי אחי, the son of רבי יאשיה, challenges his father's reading. Again he points to the exact wording of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי יאשיה's case, the slave is being sent away from ארץ ישראל. But the פסוק describes a slave coming 'to you', into the Land. So the direction of the movement in the פסוק does not match רבי יאשיה's case.

phrases.aramaic: וְקַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי אַחַי בְּרַבִּי יֹאשִׁיָּה:
phrases.english: And it was difficult for Rabbi Achai son of Rabbi Yoshiya:
This "who escapes to you"?!
It should have said "who escapes from you"!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְקַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי אַחַי בְּרַבִּי יֹאשִׁיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי יאשיה's new reading, just as רבי יאשיה attacked the first one.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יאשיה's reading: a slave sold to חוץ לארץ
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק says 'to you', meaning into the Land. A slave sold abroad is going out of the Land.

steps.title: רבי אחי: the פסוק is about a slave who runs into ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: רבי אחי ברבי יאשיה reads the פסוק as being about a slave who runs from חוץ לארץ to ארץ ישראל. He is not returned. This is the view רבי אמי relied on in the story.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי אחי ברבי יאשיה said: The פסוק is speaking about a slave who ran away from outside the Land to the Land.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אחי gives the reading that fits every word of the פסוק. This is exactly the source for רבי אמי's ruling at the start.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now 'his master' is a real master, and 'escapes to you' really means coming into ארץ ישראל. So both wording problems are solved. That is why רבי אמי told the master he could not take the slave back, and had to free him in exchange for a note.

keyTerms.meaning: from outside the Land into the Land

steps.whatToRemember: There are three readings of "לא תסגיר עבד": a גוי leaving idol worship, a slave sold to חוץ לארץ, and a slave running into ארץ ישראל. רבי אמי ruled like the last one, from רבי אחי ברבי יאשיה, so the runaway slave goes free.
steps.whyThisMatters: This closes the circle with the story. It explains why a slave who runs into ארץ ישראל cannot be taken back, and why רבי אמי let the master get paid only through a note.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי אַחַי בְּרַבִּי יֹאשִׁיָּה:
phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Achai son of Rabbi Yoshiya said:
About a slave who ran away from outside the Land to the Land
the verse is speaking.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי אַחַי בְּרַבִּי יֹאשִׁיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge to רבי יאשיה with a reading that fits all the words. It also explains the source for the ruling in step 8.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A slave who runs from חוץ לארץ into ארץ ישראל is not handed back to his master. This is the basis for רבי אמי's ruling.

steps.title: רבי reads the verse as being about a slave bought in order to be freed
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא gives רבי's reading: לא תסגיר is about a slave whose buyer bought him in order to free him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא teaches: "You shall not deliver a slave to his master." רבי says: the verse is talking about someone who buys a slave in order to free him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא that gives a fourth reading of the same פסוק. רבי says it is about a slave whose buyer meant to set him free.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the readings were about a גוי leaving idol worship, a slave sold to חוץ לארץ, and a slave running into ארץ ישראל. רבי reads the פסוק a new way. The "master" bought this slave only to free him, so the slave must not be given over to him as a slave.

keyTerms.meaning: רבי יהודה הנשיא, the editor of the משנה

phrases.english: It is taught in another ברייתא:
"You shall not deliver a slave to his master" —
phrases.notes: דברים 23:16, the same פסוק as in the earlier steps.

phrases.english: Rebbi says:
about one who buys a slave in order to free him
the verse is speaking.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא אִידַּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers another reading of the same פסוק, separate from the chain of רבי יאשיה and his son.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: לא תסגיר is about a slave bought on the condition that he will be freed. He is not handed over to the buyer.

steps.title: What exactly is the case?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי's case works in practice.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are the circumstances?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the case actually looks like. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who buys a slave owns him until he frees him. So it is unclear why the buyer has no right to him at all. The גמרא wants the exact case where the buyer never really owns him.

keyTerms.meaning: What does the case look like?

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical case behind רבי's reading.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How can a buyer have no claim on a slave he purchased?

steps.title: The slave is freed the moment he is bought
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק: the buyer wrote to the slave that once he buys him, the slave owns himself from that moment.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: he wrote to him like this: "When I buy you, you are hereby owned by yourself from now."
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers. The buyer set things up so the slave goes free at the exact moment of the purchase.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The buyer's own document frees the slave as soon as the sale happens. So the buyer never has even one moment of ownership. That is why the slave is not handed over to him.

keyTerms.meaning: You are owned by yourself, meaning you are free

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
when he wrote to him like this:
"When I buy you,
you are hereby owned by yourself from now."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The buyer wrote a document that frees the slave the moment the purchase takes effect.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי reads לא תסגיר as being about a slave who is freed the moment he is bought, through a document saying "when I buy you, you own yourself from now."

steps.title: רב חסדא's slave runs away to the כותים
steps.stepSummary: Story: רב חסדא's slave ran away to בי כותאי, and רב חסדא asked them to send him back.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא's slave ran away to בי כותאי. He sent to them: Return him to me.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story that puts the פסוק into real life. This step sets up the back-and-forth that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא asks for his runaway slave. Everything that comes next depends on how the people there understand לא תסגיר.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda's slave ran away from him
to Bei Kutai,
he sent to them: Return him to me.
phrases.notes: Some versions have the extra letter in square brackets and some don't.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חִסְדָּא עֲרַק לֵיהּ עַבְדָּא לְבֵי כוּתָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story that applies the slave פסוק in practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב חסדא asks for his runaway slave back.

steps.title: The כותים quote the verse to refuse
steps.stepSummary: The כותים answered with לא תסגיר עבד אל אדוניו.
steps.simpleTranslation: They sent to him: "You shall not deliver a slave to his master."
steps.whatsHappening: The כותים refuse to send the slave back. They quote the פסוק that says not to hand a slave over to his master.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They read the פסוק plainly: any runaway slave should not be returned. That pushes back on רב חסדא's request.

phrases.english: They sent to him:
"You shall not deliver a slave to his master."

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַחוּ לֵיהּ: לֹא תַסְגִּיר עֶבֶד אֶל אֲדוֹנָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back on רב חסדא's request.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's demand to have his slave returned
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק seems to forbid returning any runaway slave to his master.

steps.title: רב חסדא answers with the מצוה of returning lost items
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא quotes the פסוק of השבת אבידה: you must return a donkey, a garment, and anything your brother loses.
steps.simpleTranslation: He sent to them: "And so you shall do for his donkey, and so you shall do for his garment, and so you shall do for anything your brother has lost."
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers with a different פסוק, the מצוה of returning lost things. A runaway slave counts as something the owner has lost.
steps.deeperAnalysis: השבת אבידה covers "anything your brother has lost." That includes a slave who ran off. So the Torah itself requires the slave to be returned.

keyTerms.meaning: The מצוה of returning a lost item

phrases.english: He sent to them:
"And so you shall do for his donkey,
phrases.notes: דברים 22:3

phrases.english: and so you shall do for his garment,
and so you shall do for anything your brother has lost."

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַח לְהוּ: וְכֵן תַּעֲשֶׂה לַחֲמוֹרוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the כותים with a פסוק that points the other way.
steps.raayaObject: The runaway slave must be returned.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק of השבת אבידה (דברים 22:3), which covers "anything your brother has lost."

steps.title: The כותים repeat: but the verse says not to hand him over
steps.stepSummary: The כותים ask: but isn't it written לא תסגיר עבד אל אדוניו?
steps.simpleTranslation: They sent to him: But isn't it written, "You shall not deliver a slave to his master"?
steps.whatsHappening: The כותים press their point again. Even with השבת אבידה, the slave פסוק still seems to forbid returning him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now two פסוקים seem to clash. The general rule is to return lost things, but a special פסוק says not to return a slave. They argue the special פסוק should win.

phrases.english: They sent to him: But isn't it written:
"You shall not deliver a slave to his master"?

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַחוּ לֵיהּ: וְהָכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב חסדא's proof from השבת אבידה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's use of השבת אבידה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A specific פסוק about slaves seems to say the opposite of the general rule of returning lost things.

steps.title: That verse is only about a slave running into ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא: לא תסגיר is about a slave who ran from חוץ לארץ to ארץ ישראל, as רבי אחי ברבי יאשיה explained.
steps.simpleTranslation: He sent to them: That verse is about a slave who ran from outside the Land into the Land, following רבי אחי ברבי יאשיה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא narrows the slave פסוק to one case: a slave who runs into ארץ ישראל. His own slave does not fit that case, so the normal rule of returning lost things applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He uses the reading from step 13. The "don't return" rule is only for a slave escaping into ארץ ישראל. Here the slave ran from one place in חוץ לארץ to another place in חוץ לארץ, so the slave is like any other lost item and must be returned.

keyTerms.meaning: From outside the Land into the Land

phrases.english: He sent to them: That one,
phrases.notes: "That one" means the slave פסוק they quoted.

phrases.english: is about a slave who ran from outside the Land to the Land,
and following Rabbi Achai son of Rabbi Yoshiya.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַח לְהוּ: הַהוּא, בְּעֶבֶד שֶׁבָּרַח מֵחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ לָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the כותים by limiting the slave פסוק to a narrow case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: לא תסגיר forbids returning any runaway slave.
steps.terutzMaskana: לא תסגיר applies only to a slave who flees into ארץ ישראל. Other runaway slaves fall under השבת אבידה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the reading of רבי אחי ברבי יאשיה from step 13 being used in a real case.

steps.title: Why did he use רבי אחי ברבי יאשיה's reading?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב חסדא answered with that particular reading of the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is different, that he sent to them following רבי אחי ברבי יאשיה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רב חסדא picked this reading out of all the readings we saw. Other readings, like רבי's, would also have limited the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Several readings narrow the פסוק to a case that does not match רב חסדא's slave. So why choose this one in particular? The answer comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: And what is different? Why this one?

phrases.english: And what is different, that he sent to them
following Rabbi Achai son of Rabbi Yoshiya?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי שְׁנָא דִּשְׁלַח לְהוּ כִּדְרַבִּי אַחַי בְּרַבִּי יֹאשִׁיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the choice made in step 21.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רב חסדא chose this reading over the others.

steps.title: Because that reading fits the plain words of the verse
steps.stepSummary: He chose it because the כותים could see it in the פסוק itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the verses would make sense to them that way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this reading matches the simple meaning of the words. That kind of reading is what the כותים would accept.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words "he escapes to you" naturally mean running into the Land, as step 12 showed. The כותים did not go by the Sages' explanations. A reading that comes straight from the words of the פסוק was the one that could convince them.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense to them, they understand it

phrases.english: Because the verses would make sense to them that way.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּמַשְׁמַע לְהוּ קְרָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי אחי ברבי יאשיה's reading follows the plain words of the פסוק, so the כותים would accept it.
steps.whatToRemember: רב חסדא limited לא תסגיר to a slave fleeing into ארץ ישראל. He chose this reading because it fits the plain words, which the כותים would accept.

steps.title: אביי's lost donkey and the sign he gave
steps.stepSummary: אביי lost a donkey among the כותים. They asked for a סימן, and he said its belly is white.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי's donkey got lost in בי כותאי. He sent to them: Send it to me. They sent to him: Send a sign. He sent to them: Its belly is white.
steps.whatsHappening: Another story about returning a lost item to its owner. The כותים follow the normal rule and ask אביי for an identifying sign first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before you return a lost item, the claimant must give a סימן to show it is his. אביי's sign was that the donkey's belly is white. This sets up their reply in the next step.

phrases.aramaic: אַבָּיֵי אִירְכַס לֵיהּ חֲמָרָא בֵּי כוּתָאֵי,
phrases.english: Abaye's donkey got lost in Bei Kutai,
he sent to them: Send it to me.
They sent to him: Send a sign.
He sent to them: That its belly is white.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אִירְכַס לֵיהּ חֲמָרָא בֵּי כוּתָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second story about returning lost property through the כותים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone claiming a lost item must give a סימן.

steps.title: A white belly is not a real sign
steps.stepSummary: The כותים reply that they are returning it only because he is נחמני, since all donkeys have white bellies.
steps.simpleTranslation: They sent to him: If you were not נחמני, we would not send it to you. Don't all donkeys have white bellies?!
steps.whatsHappening: The כותים point out that אביי's sign proves nothing. They return the donkey only because they trust him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A sign only counts if it sets this item apart from others. Every donkey has a white belly, so this sign is worthless. The donkey came back only because of אביי's personal trustworthiness, not because of the sign.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say? (a rhetorical challenge)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't take this as a ruling that you return a lost item on any sign at all. The כותים are saying the opposite: this sign was worthless, and they returned the donkey only because they trusted אביי.
steps.whatToRemember: A real סימן must set the item apart. A sign that every item of that kind has, like a donkey's white belly, does not count.

phrases.english: They sent to him:
If not for the fact that you are Nachmani,
phrases.notes: נחמני is אביי's own name. They mean: we know you, so we trust you.

phrases.english: we would not send it to you;
is that to say that all donkeys
don't have white bellies?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי לָאו דְּנַחְמָנִי אַתְּ, לָא הֲוָה מְשַׁדַּרְנָא לֵיהּ נִיהֲלָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the sign אביי gave in step 24.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A white belly is common to all donkeys, so it does not identify this donkey.

steps.title: The משנה: no ransom above a captive's value
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that captives are not redeemed for more than their market value, because of תיקון העולם.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: We do not redeem captives for more than their value, because of the betterment of the world.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens with a rule about ransoming Jewish captives. We may not pay more than the captive is really worth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though freeing captives is a great מצוה, the חכמים put a ceiling on the price. The reason given is תיקון העולם, a general good for society. The משנה does not explain what that good is, and the גמרא asks about this in step 29.

keyTerms.meaning: Their value (what they would sell for)
The betterment of the world, a rule made for the good of society

phrases.english: MISHNA:
We do not redeem the captives
for more than their value,
because of the betterment of the world.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין פּוֹדִין אֶת הַשְּׁבוּיִין יָתֵר עַל כְּדֵי דְּמֵיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. It ends the earlier discussion about slaves and the כותים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Captives may not be ransomed for more than their value, because of תיקון העולם.

steps.title: The משנה: no helping captives escape
steps.stepSummary: The משנה adds that we do not help captives escape from their captors, also because of תיקון העולם.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we do not help the captives escape, because of the betterment of the world.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second rule. We may not smuggle captives out of captivity, and again the reason is תיקון העולם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Helping a captive run away sounds kind, but it can make things worse. Captors may guard their captives more harshly in the future. The תנא קמא files this under the same general reason, תיקון העולם.

phrases.english: And we do not help the captives escape,
because of the betterment of the world.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין מַבְרִיחִין אֶת הַשְּׁבוּיִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second rule about captives, with the same reason.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may not help captives escape, because of תיקון העולם.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's different reason
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says the reason is תקנת השבויין, the good of the captives themselves.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: Because of the betterment of the captives.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל gives a different reason for the rule. He says it is for the good of the captives, not the world in general.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He agrees with the rule but changes its reason. In his view the worry is for other captives, who could suffer because of an escape. A different reason can lead to different results in borderline cases.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא, נשיא of the generation
The good or protection of the captives

steps.confusionAlert: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is not saying you may help captives escape. He accepts the rule and only argues about the reason behind it.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
Because of the betterment of the captives.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: מִפְּנֵי תַּקָּנַת הַשְּׁבוּיִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the תנא קמא about the reason for the rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The reason for the rule is the protection of the captives, תקנת השבויין.

steps.title: What does 'betterment of the world' mean for ransom?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the ransom limit protects the community from financial strain, or stops kidnappers from capturing more Jews.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: A question was asked: This phrase 'because of the betterment of the world', is it because of the financial pressure on the community? Or perhaps it is so that they will not seize and bring more captives?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its discussion with an איבעיא. It wants to know the exact reason behind the ransom limit in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two choices. One is דוחקא דצבורא, meaning the community could not afford sky-high ransoms. The other is that big payments would encourage kidnappers to grab more Jews. The answer matters for a private person paying with his own money. The first reason would not stop him, but the second would.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked before them (a real open question)
The financial pressure on the community

steps.whyThisMatters: The two reasons give different rulings when a relative wants to pay a huge ransom from his own pocket.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
A question was asked before them:
This phrase 'because of the betterment of the world':
is it because of the financial pressure on the community,
or perhaps it is because
they should not seize and bring more captives?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: הַאי מִפְּנֵי תִּיקּוּן הָעוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the reason given in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the ransom limit based on protecting the community's money, or on removing the kidnappers' incentive?

steps.title: Proof from Levi bar Darga's huge ransom
steps.stepSummary: לוי בר דרגא redeemed his daughter for 13,000 gold dinars, which suggests the limit is only about community funds.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: לוי בר דרגא redeemed his daughter for thirteen thousand gold dinars.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story to answer the question. A man paid a huge private ransom for his daughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the rule were meant to stop kidnappers, a private person could not overpay either. Since לוי בר דרגא did overpay, the rule seems to be only about דוחקא דצבורא. That kind of worry would not apply to his own money.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear, introducing a proof
A man who paid a large ransom for his daughter

phrases.english: Come and hear:
that Levi bar Darga redeemed his daughter
for thirteen thousand gold dinars.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: דְּלֵוִי בַּר דַּרְגָּא פַּרְקַהּ לִבְרַתֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to settle the איבעיא from a real case.
steps.raayaObject: That the ransom limit is because of דוחקא דצבורא
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of לוי בר דרגא paying 13,000 gold dinars

steps.title: אביי: maybe he went against the Sages
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects the proof, because לוי בר דרגא may have acted without the approval of the חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: And who told us that he acted with the approval of the Sages? Perhaps he acted against the approval of the Sages.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on the proof. A story about what one person did does not show that it was allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof only works if the חכמים agreed to what לוי בר דרגא did. אביי says maybe they did not, so his act tells us nothing about the law. That means the question is still open.

keyTerms.meaning: With the approval of the Sages
And who will tell us? (who says?)

steps.whatToRemember: The question of why we limit ransom (community money vs. the kidnappers' incentive) is not settled here. A private person's act is no proof unless the חכמים approved it.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
And who will tell us
that he acted with the approval of the Sages?
Perhaps he acted against the approval of the Sages.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: וּמַאן לֵימָא לַן דְּבִרְצוֹן חֲכָמִים עֲבַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 30.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from לוי בר דרגא. It does not decide the איבעיא either way.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumes his act was approved by the חכמים, but he may have acted against their wishes.

steps.title: What is the practical difference between the two reasons?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule against helping captives escape, along with its two reasons, and asks what practical difference there is between them.
steps.simpleTranslation: We do not help captives escape, because of תיקון העולם. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: because of תקנת השבויין. What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה again so that it can ask a question about it. It wants to know when the two reasons would lead to different results.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions agree that we do not help captives escape. They give different reasons. The גמרא assumes that two different reasons must lead to different rulings in at least some case, so it asks what that case is.

keyTerms.meaning: Help someone escape or run away
The good of the captives themselves
What is the difference between them?

phrases.english: And we do not help the captives escape
because of the betterment of the world.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
because of the betterment of captives.
What is the difference between them?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה's rule about captive escape, after the side discussion about ransom limits.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In what case does the reason of תיקון העולם lead to a different ruling than the reason of תקנת השבויין?

steps.title: The difference: when there is only one captive
steps.stepSummary: The two reasons give different results when there is only one captive.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them when there is only one captive.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. The two opinions disagree in a case where only one captive is being held.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, the worry is that the kidnappers will take revenge on the captives left behind. If there is only one captive, nobody is left behind, so we may help him escape. According to the תנא קמא, the worry is that kidnappers in general will start guarding captives more harshly, and that is still a concern with one captive.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them

steps.whatToRemember: With only one captive, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל would allow helping him escape, because no other captives will suffer. The תנא קמא would still forbid it, because of the effect on how captives are treated in the future.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them,
where there is only one.
phrases.notes: He means only one captive, so nobody else is left behind to suffer when he escapes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 32.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The two reasons differ when there is only one captive.

steps.title: רב נחמן's daughters stir a boiling pot with their hands
steps.stepSummary: A story begins: the daughters of רב נחמן would stir a boiling pot with their bare hands.
steps.simpleTranslation: The daughters of רב נחמן would stir a pot with their hands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story connected to captives. This first line sets up the story: רב נחמן's daughters stirred a hot pot with their bare hands and were not burned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People took this as a sign that the daughters were very righteous, as if the heat could not harm them. That impression is what leads to רב עילישׁ's question in the next step.

phrases.english: The daughters of Rav Nachman
would stir a pot with their hands.
phrases.notes: This means a boiling pot, stirred with bare hands and no spoon.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּנָתֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן בָּחֲשָׁן קִדְרָא בִּידַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new story about captives, after the legal discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The daughters of רב נחמן seemed so righteous that boiling heat did not hurt them.

steps.title: רב עילישׁ's difficulty with a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רב עילישׁ is bothered by a פסוק that says a good woman cannot be found, since רב נחמן's daughters seem to be such women.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עילישׁ had a difficulty. It is written: 'One man in a thousand I found, but a woman among all these I did not find.' But there are the daughters of רב נחמן!
steps.whatsHappening: רב עילישׁ raises a difficulty with a פסוק. The פסוק seems to say no truly good woman can be found, yet רב נחמן's daughters look exactly like such women.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'proof' against the פסוק comes from the miracle with the pot in the previous step. רב עילישׁ assumes the miracle shows they are righteous, so the פסוק seems to be wrong about them.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a formal challenge in a legal debate. It is רב עילישׁ's own question, and the story goes on to show that his assumption about the daughters may have been mistaken.

phrases.english: Rav Ilish had a difficulty,
it is written:
"One man out of a thousand I have found,
phrases.notes: קהלת 7:28

phrases.english: but a woman among all these I have not found,"
but there are the daughters of Rav Nachman!

steps.triggerLanguage: קַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ לְרַב עִילִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the miracle of step 34 to question a פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: The פסוק in קהלת saying a good woman cannot be found.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב נחמן's daughters seem to be exactly such good women, so the פסוק appears to be contradicted.

steps.title: The daughters and רב עילישׁ are taken captive
steps.stepSummary: Because of what was said, the daughters were taken captive, and רב עילישׁ was taken captive with them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The matter caused them to be taken captive, and he was also taken captive with them.
steps.whatsHappening: The story moves forward. The daughters are taken captive, and רב עילישׁ is captured together with them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words spoken about the daughters somehow caused their captivity. This sets up the scene for the rest of the story, which takes place in captivity.

phrases.english: The matter caused them, and they were taken captive,
phrases.notes: Literally 'the matter caused for them.' The words spoken about them led to their capture.

phrases.english: and he was also taken captive with them.

steps.triggerLanguage: גְּרַמָא לְהוּ מִילְּתָא וְאִשְׁתַּבְיָין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tells what happened after רב עילישׁ's comment.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב נחמן's daughters and רב עילישׁ were taken captive.

steps.title: The raven says to escape, but רב עילישׁ does not trust it
steps.stepSummary: A man who understood bird language told רב עילישׁ that a raven was saying 'עילישׁ, escape.' רב עילישׁ refused to rely on a lying raven.
steps.simpleTranslation: One day a man who knew the language of birds was sitting with him. A raven came and called to him. He asked: What is it saying? The man said: 'עילישׁ, escape; עילישׁ, escape.' He said: A raven is a liar, and I do not rely on it.
steps.whatsHappening: In captivity, a raven seems to tell רב עילישׁ to escape. He does not act on it, because he considers ravens untrustworthy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This connects to the משנה's topic of captives escaping. רב עילישׁ will not risk escaping based on a sign he cannot trust.

phrases.aramaic: יוֹמָא חַד הֲוָה יָתֵיב גַּבֵּיהּ הָהוּא גַּבְרָא,
phrases.english: One day a certain man was sitting with him,
who knew the language of birds.
A raven came and was calling to him.
He said to him: What is it saying?
phrases.notes: רב עילישׁ is asking the man who understands birds.

phrases.english: He said to him: "Ilish, escape; Ilish, escape."
He said: A raven is a liar,
and I do not rely on it.

steps.triggerLanguage: יוֹמָא חַד הֲוָה יָתֵיב גַּבֵּיהּ הָהוּא גַּבְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the captivity story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב עילישׁ will not escape based on the raven's message, because a raven is not trustworthy.

steps.title: The dove says to escape, and רב עילישׁ sees a sign of a miracle
steps.stepSummary: A dove gives the same message. רב עילישׁ trusts it, because the Jewish people are compared to a dove, and concludes that a miracle will happen for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Meanwhile a dove came and was calling. He asked: What is it saying? The man said: 'עילישׁ, escape; עילישׁ, escape.' He said: The Jewish people are compared to a dove. This shows a miracle will happen for me.
steps.whatsHappening: Now a dove gives the same message to escape. This time רב עילישׁ trusts it and understands that he will be helped by a miracle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The message is the same, but the messenger is different. Because the dove is a symbol of the Jewish people, רב עילישׁ treats its message as a trustworthy sign.

keyTerms.meaning: The Jewish people as a whole

phrases.english: Meanwhile a dove came and was calling.
He said to him: What is it saying?
He said to him: "Ilish, escape; Ilish, escape."
He said: The Congregation of Israel is compared to a dove,
conclude from this that a miracle will happen for me.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַדְּהָכִי אֲתָא יוֹנָה וְקָא קָרְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts the trustworthy dove with the raven of step 37.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because the dove stands for the Jewish people, רב עילישׁ trusts its message and expects a miracle.

steps.title: רב עילישׁ decides to check on רב נחמן's daughters
steps.stepSummary: Before escaping, רב עילישׁ decides to see whether רב נחמן's daughters stayed faithful. If they did, he will bring them back home.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: I will go and see the daughters of רב נחמן. If they have stayed firm in their faith, I will bring them back.
steps.whatsHappening: רב עילישׁ does not just run away alone. He plans to check on the daughters first, and this sets up the next part of the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His plan to bring them home depends on one condition: whether they have stayed faithful during their captivity. This also ties back to his earlier question about whether they are truly righteous.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר: אֵיזִיל אֶחְזֵי בְּנָתֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן,
phrases.english: He said: I will go and see the daughters of Rav Nachman,
if they are standing firm in their faith, I will bring them back.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיזִיל אֶחְזֵי בְּנָתֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After deciding to escape, רב עילישׁ plans to check on the daughters first.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב עילישׁ will bring the daughters home only if they have stayed faithful.

steps.title: רב עילישׁ plans to listen to the women in private
steps.stepSummary: רב עילישׁ reasons that women share their secrets with each other in the bathroom, so that is where he can learn what the daughters really think.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: Women tell each other all their private matters in the bathroom.
steps.whatsHappening: רב עילישׁ figures out how he can test the daughters' loyalty, which he decided to do in step 39. This sets up the next step, where he overhears them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He needs to hear what the daughters say when they think no one is listening. A private place is where their true feelings will come out, so he plans to listen there.

keyTerms.meaning: they lay out, they tell over

phrases.english: He said: Women
all matters that they have
they tell over to each other in the bathroom.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר: נְשֵׁי, כׇּל מִילֵּי דְּאִית לְהוּ סָדְרָן לַהֲדָדֵי בְּבֵית הַכִּסֵּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Carries out his plan from step 39 to check whether the daughters stayed faithful.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב עילישׁ reasons that he can learn the women's true feelings by listening to their private talk.

steps.title: The daughters want to stay with their captors
steps.stepSummary: רב עילישׁ overhears the daughters say that they now see their captors as husbands, and that they want to be moved away so they won't be found and redeemed.
steps.simpleTranslation: He heard them saying: These men are our husbands, and the men of נהרדעא are husbands too. Let's tell our captors to take us far from here, so that our people don't come, hear about us, and redeem us.
steps.whatsHappening: The test gives its answer: the daughters did not stay faithful. They would rather stay with their captors.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 39 רב עילישׁ said he would bring them home only if they stayed faithful. Now he hears that they don't even want to be rescued, so he has no reason to take them with him.

phrases.english: He heard them saying:
These are husbands
phrases.notes: "These" means the captors standing right there with them.

phrases.english: and the men of Nehardea are husbands,
let us tell our captors
to take us far from here,
so that people don't come and hear
and redeem us.

steps.triggerLanguage: שַׁמְעִינְהוּ דְּקָאָמְרָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the result of the listening plan from step 40.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The daughters prefer to stay with their captors and do not want to be redeemed.

steps.title: רב עילישׁ escapes by a miracle
steps.stepSummary: רב עילישׁ runs away together with the man who understood birds. A miracle lets רב עילישׁ cross the river on a ferry, but the other man is caught and killed.
steps.simpleTranslation: He got up and ran away. He and that man came along. For him a miracle happened, and he crossed on a ferry. That man was found and killed.
steps.whatsHappening: רב עילישׁ escapes without the daughters, together with the man who understood birds. The miracle he expected in step 38 comes true for him, but the other man is caught and killed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 38 he trusted the dove and expected a miracle. Now it happens for him, but not for the other man. The story shows that the miracle was meant for רב עילישׁ himself.

phrases.english: He got up and ran away,
he and that man came along.
phrases.notes: "That man" is the one who understood bird language, from step 37.

phrases.english: For him, a miracle happened
and he crossed on a ferry,
and that man, they found him and killed him.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָם, עֲרַק, אֲתָא אִיהוּ וְהָהוּא גַּבְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finding out the daughters were not faithful, he escapes without them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב עילישׁ escapes through a miracle, as he predicted, while his companion is killed.

steps.title: The pot miracle was witchcraft, not righteousness
steps.stepSummary: When the daughters come home, רב עילישׁ explains that they could stir the boiling pot without getting burned because of witchcraft. So they were not the righteous women he had thought.
steps.simpleTranslation: When they came back home, he said: They used to stir the pot with witchcraft.
steps.whatsHappening: רב עילישׁ closes the story by answering his own question from step 35.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 35 the daughters seemed to prove the פסוק wrong, because they looked like righteous women. Now רב עילישׁ shows that their 'miracle' came from witchcraft, so the פסוק stands without a problem.
steps.whatToRemember: The story's lesson: the daughters' apparent miracle came from witchcraft, so רב עילישׁ's question on the פסוק is answered.

phrases.english: When they returned and came back, he said:
phrases.notes: "They" are רב נחמן's daughters, who were later freed and came home.

phrases.english: They used to stir the pot with witchcraft.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הָדְרָן וְאָתָן, אֲמַר: הֲווֹ קָא בָחֲשָׁן קִידְרָא בִּכְשָׁפִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the story and answers the question raised in step 35.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The daughters' ability to stir the boiling pot came from witchcraft, so it does not show they were righteous, and the פסוק is not contradicted.

steps.title: Do not overpay non-Jews for holy objects
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה rules that we do not buy ספרי תורה, תפילין, or מזוזות from non-Jews for more than they are worth.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: We do not buy ספרים, תפילין, or מזוזות from non-Jews for more than their value.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא's story is finished, and a new משנה begins. It starts a new rule about buying back holy objects from non-Jews.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This rule follows the pattern of the earlier משנה about not redeeming captives for more than their value. Now the same limit is applied to holy objects. The sentence continues on the next amud.

phrases.english: MISHNA: And we do not buy scrolls,
tefillin, or mezuzot from the non-Jews
for more than their value,

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ וְאֵין לוֹקְחִין סְפָרִים, תְּפִילִּין וּמְזוּזוֹת מִן הַגּוֹיִם יוֹתֵר עַל כְּדֵי דְמֵיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the story behind and opens a new משנה with a new rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: We do not pay non-Jews more than market value to buy back ספרים, תפילין, or מזוזות.
